Entry Into a Material Definitive Agreement. The Merger On November 1, 2026, Marvell Technology, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Marvell ”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with Lumentum Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Lumentum ”), Java Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“ Merger Sub I ”) and Java Merger Sub II, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“ Merger Sub II ” and together with Merger Sub I, each a “ Merger Sub ” and collectively the “ Merger Subs ”). Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Lumentum (the “ First Merger ”), with Lumentum continuing as the surviving corporation (the “ Surviving Corporation ”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the “ Second Merger ” and, collectively or in seriatim with the First Merger, as applicable, the “ Merger ”), with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving corporation of the Second Merger (the “ Second Surviving Corporation ”). The board of directors of Marvell (the “ Marvell Board ”) has unanimously: (i) approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, an amendment of Marvell’s Second Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the “ Charter ”) to increase the number of authorized shares of Marvell Common Stock thereunder (the “ Charter Amendment ”), the issuance of the shares of Marvell Common Stock and, if applicable, Marvell Series B Preferred Stock, in connection with the Merger (the “ Share Issuance ”), (ii) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Merger, the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance, are fair to, and in the best interests of, Marvell and its stockholders, and (iii) resolved to recommend that Marvell’s stockholders approve the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance. Merger Consideration At the effective time of the First Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum (the “ Lumentum Common Stock ”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of common stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “ Marvell Common Stock ,” and such ratio, the “ Exchange Ratio ”), with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “ Common Stock Merger Consideration ”). At the Effective Time, each share of preferred stock, par value $0.001 per share, of Lumentum designated as Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “ Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock ” and, together with the Lumentum Common Stock, the “ Lumentum Capital Stock ”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Marvell Common Stock equal to the product of (a) the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock into which such share of Lumentum Preferred Stock is convertible pursuant to its terms as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (b) the Exchange Ratio, with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “ Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration ”). However, if a holder of shares of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock makes an election in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement to receive the Merger Consideration in the form of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “ Marvell Series B Preferred Stock ,” and such election, a “ Preferred Stock Election ”), then each share of Lumentum Preferred Stock that is held by such holder immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be converted into the right to receive one share of Marvell Series B Preferred Stock (the “ Series B Preferred Stock Merger Consideration ” and together with the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration and the Common Stock Merger Consideration, the “ Merger Consideration ”). The Marvell Series B Preferred Stock is intended to have the same terms and rights as the Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock, except that each share is convertible for the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration.   The shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Merger will be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“ Nasdaq ”). In connection with the issuance of the Merger Consideration by Marvell, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the date of the Merger Agreement, Marvell and Lumentum will jointly prepare and cause to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”) a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “ Form S-4 ”), which will include the joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum for their respective meetings of stockholders relating to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement. Treatment of Equity Awards Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, each Lumentum equity award, consisting of stock options, restricted stock units and performance stock units, that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be converted into an equivalent Marvell equity award, including with respect to vesting conditions (including termination protection and provisions, expiration and post-termination exercisability), except that performance stock units will be converted into solely time-vesting restricted stock units. The number of shares of Marvell Common Stock subject to each converted equity award will be equal to the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock then subject to the award (with the number of shares subject to any performance stock unit determined based on (i) the greater of target and actual performance levels for stock price performance metrics and (ii) except as otherwise provided by the terms of Lumentum’s Change in Control and Severance Benefits Plan, as amended and restated, that would apply assuming a participant’s qualifying termination of employment upon the consummation of the Merger, at projected actual performance for all other performance metrics measured through the Effective Time), multiplied by the Exchange Ratio, and the exercise price of each converted stock option will be equal to the exercise price of the Lumentum stock option divided by the Exchange Ratio. Form 20-F ☒ Form 40-F ☐ On November 3, 2026, the Registrant and Innolight Announce Advancing High-Performance Near-Package Optics for AI Infrastructure SIGNATURES Pursuant to the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the registrant has duly caused this report to be signed on its behalf by the undersigned, thereunto duly authorized. TOWER SEMICONDUCTOR LTD. Date: November 3, 2026 By: /s/ Nati Somekh Name: Nati Somekh Title: Corporate Secretary Tower Semiconductor and Innolight Advance High-Performance Near-Package Optics for AI Infrastructure Leveraging Tower's 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics platforms, the collaboration supports multiple generations of Near-Packaged Optics development for AI infrastructure MIGDAL HAEMEK, Israel and SUZHOU, China, November 3, 2026 – Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM), the leading foundry for high-value analog semiconductor solutions, and Innolight, a leading provider of optical connectivity solutions for data center and AI infrastructure applications, today announced their continued collaboration on emerging Near-Package Optics (NPO) applications. The collaboration combines Innolight's expertise in optical interconnect solutions with Tower's high-volume 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics manufacturing platforms to address the increasing performance and bandwidth requirements of next-generation AI infrastructure. Leveraging Tower's high-volume 200mm and 300mm Silicon Photonics platforms, Innolight has achieved a key milestone in the development of its Near-Package Optics (NPO) portfolio with its first NPO device entering early production using Tower's PH18M Silicon Photonics process flow running in Tower’s US CA factory. In parallel, Innolight has taped-out multiple NPO products on Tower's 300mm Silicon Photonics platform to support future product generations. As AI workloads continue to scale, NPO architectures are emerging as one of the preferred approaches for next-generation optical interconnects. These emerging architectures are expected to drive additional demand beyond today's pluggable optical module market, driving the new phase of optical interconnect solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. "Near-Package Optics is emerging as a key technology for next-generation AI and cloud infrastructure," said Oliver Sun, CTO of Innolight . "Our collaboration with Tower provides us with industry leading capabilities enabling us to accelerate the development of NPO solutions to meet the evolving needs of hyperscale and AI data center customers." NPO architectures typically require substantially higher optical channel counts than conventional pluggable optical modules, often integrating 16 or more channels on a single device. As channel counts increase, manufacturing expertise, process control, and yield performance become increasingly critical. Tower's leadership in high-volume Silicon Photonics manufacturing and its advanced 200mm and 300mm SiPho platforms provide the process uniformity, high-yield performance, and rich device offerings needed to support these increasingly complex designs. The platform also enables monolithic integration of multiple photonic functions, including wavelength division multiplexing and demultiplexing on a single chip, enabling increased functionality with compact size while optimizing performance and scalability. “Given their market and product leadership, Innolight continues to be a critical technology partner for Tower’s silicon photonics roadmap as well as cornerstone manufacturing customer now across four of our facilities, two in the US (Newport Beach California and San Antonio Texas) and one each in Israel and Japan,” said Dr. Marco Racanelli, President, Tower Semiconductor. “By combining Innolight's innovation in optical connectivity with Tower's differentiated Silicon Photonics technologies and manufacturing expertise, we continue to advance solutions that address the demands of future optical networks.” For additional information about Tower Semiconductor’s SiPho platform, visit here . For additional information about Innolight, please visit here . About Innolight InnoLight is a world leader in providing a wide range of high-speed optical solutions for optical communication networking, especially for AI and Data Center applications, with global footprints in California, Singapore, Thailand, and Taiwan and Suzhou China. For more information, please visit www.innolight.com. About Tower Semiconductor Tower Semiconductor Ltd. (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM) is a leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, serving growing markets including industrial, automotive, mobile, infrastructure, medical, and aerospace & defense. The company offers a broad portfolio of advanced and innovative analog technologies, including silicon photonics (SiPho), SiGe, RF CMOS, CMOS image sensors, power management, and mixed-signal, supported by world-class design enablement and process transfer services. Tower operates a global manufacturing network with 200mm and 300mm fabs in Israel, the U.S., Japan, and Italy, providing customers with scalable capacity and multi-fab sourcing. Learn more at: www.towersemi.com . Safe Harbor Regarding Forward-Looking Statements This press release includes forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. On October 23, 2026, Evernorth Holdings Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Company”), entered into a Common Stock Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with CF Principal Investments LLC (“Cantor”) relating to a committed equity facility (the “Facility”). Pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, the Company has the right from time to time at its option to sell to Cantor up to 5,218,935 newly issued shares (the “Total Commitment”) of the Company’s Class A common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the “Common Stock”), subject to certain conditions and limitations set forth in the Purchase Agreement. While there are distinct differences, the Facility is structured similarly to a traditional at-the-market equity facility, insofar as it allows the Company to raise primary equity capital on a periodic basis outside the context of a traditional underwritten follow-on offering. Sales of the Common Stock to Cantor under the Purchase Agreement, and the timing of any sales, will be determined by the Company from time to time in its sole discretion and will depend on a variety of factors, including, among other things, market conditions, the trading price of the Common Stock and determinations by the Company regarding the use of proceeds of such Common Stock. The net proceeds from any sales under the Purchase Agreement will depend on the frequency with, and prices at, which the Common Stock is sold to Cantor. The Company expects to use the proceeds from any sales under the Purchase Agreement in the manner to be set forth in the prospectus included in the Initial Resale Registration Statement (as defined below). Upon the initial satisfaction of the conditions to Cantor’s obligation to purchase Common Stock set forth in the Purchase Agreement (the “Commencement”), including that a registration statement registering the resale by Cantor of the Common Stock under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), that may be sold to it by the Company under the Purchase Agreement (the “Initial Resale Registration Statement”) is declared effective by the SEC and a final prospectus relating thereto is filed with the SEC, the Company will have the right, but not the obligation, from time to time at its sole discretion until the first day of the month next following the 14-month anniversary of the date of the Purchase Agreement, to direct Cantor to purchase shares of Common Stock by delivering written notice to Cantor after 6:00 a.m., New York City time, but prior to 9:00 a.m., New York City time, on any trading day. The number of shares that Cantor may be required to purchase pursuant to any such notice is limited to the least of (i) the number of shares that, when aggregated with all other shares of Common Stock then beneficially owned by Cantor and its affiliates, would not result in their beneficial ownership of more than 4.99% of the outstanding voting power or shares of Common Stock (the “Beneficial Ownership Limitation”), (ii) 20% of the total number of shares of Common Stock traded during the applicable purchase period on the applicable purchase date and (iii) the Company’s good faith estimate, set forth in the notice, of the number of shares Cantor will be obligated to purchase. The purchase price of the shares of Common Stock that the Company elects to sell to Cantor pursuant to the Purchase Agreement will be 97% of the volume weighted average price of the Common Stock during the applicable purchase period on the purchase date on which the Company has timely delivered written notice to Cantor directing it to purchase Common Stock under the Purchase Agreement; provided that, on any trading day on which the Company delivers, and Cantor accepts, a notice requesting a percentage of trading volume in excess of 20%, the purchase price will be calculated using the lower of such volume weighted average price and the lowest sale price in any block trade of more than 100,000 shares sold on such trading day following such acceptance. In addition, the Company may not deliver a purchase notice unless the closing sale price of the Common Stock on the immediately preceding trading day is not less than a threshold price equal to the greater of (a) $1.00, (b) 90% of such closing sale price and (c) such higher price as the Company may specify in the notice (the “Threshold Price”), and if the sale price of the Common Stock falls below the Threshold Price during a purchase date, the number of shares purchased and the purchase price will be calculated using only the portion of such purchase date during which the sale price was not below the Threshold Price. In consideration for Cantor’s execution and delivery of the Purchase Agreement, the Company agreed to pay to Cantor a cash commitment fee of $521,893.50, equal to 1.0% of the Total Commitment multiplied by $10.00 per share (the “Upfront Commitment Fee”), by wire transfer of immediately available funds within five business days following the Upfront Determination Date specified in the Purchase Agreement. The “Upfront Determination Date” is the date on which the Initial Resale Registration Statement is declared effective by the SEC. The entire amount of the Upfront Commitment Fee will be fully earned by Cantor and non-refundable as of the date of the Purchase Agreement, regardless of whether any purchases are made or settled under the Purchase Agreement or of any subsequent termination of the Purchase Agreement; provided that, on the earliest of (x) the date Cantor has purchased 1,000,000 shares of Common Stock under the Purchase Agreement, (y) the date that is eight weeks after the Upfront Determination Date and (z) the effective date of any termination of the Purchase Agreement by the Company, including in connection with the engagement of Cantor Fitzgerald & Co. for an at the market offering pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Agreement (the “Measurement Date”), the fee will be recalculated as 1.0% of the Total Commitment multiplied by the volume weighted average price at which the first 1,000,000 shares of Common Stock purchased under the Purchase Agreement through the Measurement Date were purchased, before giving effect to any discount applied in determining the purchase price (the “True-Up Fee”), or, if no shares have been purchased as of the Measurement Date, multiplied by the closing sale price of the Common Stock on the Upfront Determination Date. To the extent the True-Up Fee exceeds the Upfront Commitment Fee, the Company must pay such excess amount (the “Additional Commitment Fee”) to Cantor in cash within three trading days after the Measurement Date or, where the Measurement Date occurs by reason of clause (z) above, on or before the effective date of such termination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall the aggregate amount of Upfront Commitment Fee plus any Additional Commitment Fee payable by the Company to Cantor exceed $1,000,000. For the avoidance of doubt, the Upfront Commitment Fee will not be reduced if the recalculated amount is less than the Upfront Commitment Fee, and any Additional Commitment Fee will form part of the Upfront Commitment Fee for all purposes of the Purchase Agreement. Additionally, if during the term of the Facility the Company becomes eligible to register the Common Stock on Form S-3, the Company may, at its sole option, terminate the Purchase Agreement and engage Cantor Fitzgerald & Co. as its exclusive sales agent for an “at the market offering” as defined in Rule 4
